title: Scheduler reordering causing cross-model TTFT spikes — mitigation and customer communication
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported multi-second jumps in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and a sustained drop in tokens/sec after deployment of runtime-1.21. Investigation points to a new scheduler reordering heuristic that mixes short interactive chats across model variants on the same worker, causing KV cache churn and suboptimal kernel selection paths.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile TTFT for affected model families returns to within 10% of pre-1.21 baseline on Hosted and Dedicated
Tokens/sec recovers to baseline during 10-minute steady-state load tests
Affected customers confirm visible improvement in production test windows
Feature-flagged change deployed and monitored with rollback button verified
steps_taken: 11/12: PagerDuty triggered by on-call after alerting: hosted/region-us-west-2 95p TTFT +2.1s; initial triage assigned to runtime team
11/12: Correlated spikes to requests that route across multiple model variants; KV cache miss-rate increased ~6x on workers running mixed-model queues (observed in per-worker metrics)
11/13: Reproduced locally with synthetic traffic that interleaves small chat requests across model-v1 and model-v2; confirmed KV cache thrash + recompile path activation causing CPU stalls
11/14: Narrowed root cause to scheduler.reorder_v2 heuristic introduced in runtime-1.21 which tries aggressive request interleaving to improve throughput for long-running batches
11/14: Deployed emergency config toggles for affected Dedicated clusters to pin model-affinity; reduced 95p TTFT by ~1.6s in canary
11/15: Prepared code patch to add conservative batching timeout and model-affinity pinning per worker, plus feature flag gating
11/16: Ran load tests against Hosted staging: 30m steady-state with mixed-model distribution; tokens/sec recovered to 97% baseline and 95p TTFT within 8% of baseline
11/17: Notified affected customers (Customer A - Dedicated, Customer B - Private) with mitigation timeline and temporary config changes; Customer support drafting follow-up notes
proposed_fix: Introduce conservative scheduler mode: disable aggressive interleaving by default, add worker-level model-affinity windows (configurable TTL), and minor kernel-selection guard that avoids kernel fallback during short sequences. Ship behind feature flag scheduler.reorder_v2 (default=false).
rollback_plan: If regressions occur after rollout, flip scheduler.reorder_v2=false cluster-wide, revert config changes via orchestration-runbook (runbooks/rollback-scheduler.md), and open emergency incident meeting. Dedicated customers can be toggled individually via fleet-config API.
communication_notes: 11/15 09:20 UTC: Sent interim update to affected customers — temporary model-affinity pinned; ETA for full fix ~72h
11/16 17:40 UTC: Post-canary status to #customer-ops; no new escalations after canary adjustments
11/18 11:00 UTC: Preparing customer-facing postmortem draft and technical RCA for internal review
risks_and_tradeoffs: Conservative scheduler reduces interleaving which may slightly reduce aggregate throughput for long-batch workloads (expected 3–6% TPS impact)
Worker-level affinity increases remote resource utilization and could increase tail latency for very large batch-only jobs if misconfigured
Feature-flag complexity: leaving reorder_v2=false for too long preserves safety but delays throughput improvements planned in runtime-1.21
next_steps: Finish code review and merge PR #4218 with feature flag and unit tests
Deploy to Hosted canary pool (region us-west-2) and monitor 95p TTFT, tokens/sec, and KV cache miss-rate for 24h
Coordinate Dedicated customer rollouts with SRE and Account Engineering for per-tenant toggles
Publish internal RCA and customer-facing incident summary; schedule postmortem presentation next week
